edges.description: Loss of sulfur dioxygenase activity prevents catabolism of sulfide, so H2S and its metabolite thiosulfate accumulate to toxic levels.
H2S inhibits and accelerates degradation of cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV).
H2S inhibition of short-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase / short-chain fatty acid oxidation produces the ethylmalonic aciduria and C4/C5 acylcarnitine elevation that define the biochemical phenotype.
The vasoactive/vasotoxic action of H2S on the endothelium of small vessels produces the microangiopathy underlying petechiae and orthostatic acrocyanosis.
Accumulation of H2S in the colonic mucosa drives the chronic diarrhea characteristic of the disease.
Systemic sulfide toxicity with chronic hemorrhagic diarrhea, vomiting, and oropharyngeal swallowing difficulties impairs caloric retention and growth.
Gastrointestinal mucosal and systemic sulfide intoxication provokes recurrent infantile vomiting in a subset of patients.
Cerebral energy failure from complex IV deficiency (together with direct neurotoxicity of sulfide) drives the encephalopathy, psychomotor regression and symmetric basal ganglia lesions.
Impaired short-chain fatty acid oxidation leads to marked urinary excretion of ethylmalonic acid.
Small-vessel microangiopathy produces relapsing petechiae.
Vasomotor instability produces orthostatic acrocyanosis.
Progressive metabolic encephalopathy causes loss of acquired psychomotor milestones.
Early-onset cerebral injury impairs motor and speech milestone acquisition.
Surviving children exhibit mild-to-severe cognitive impairment from chronic encephalopathy.
Early cerebral and neuromuscular bioenergetic dysfunction manifests with generalized infantile hypotonia.
Corticospinal tract injury produces progressive hypertonia and spastic pyramidal signs.
Basal ganglia necrotic and bioenergetic injury produces extrapyramidal dystonia.
Cerebral sulfide neurotoxicity and complex IV energy failure provoke generalized tonic-clonic seizures.
Selective vulnerability of the striatum/basal ganglia to COX inhibition and microvascular injury produces T2 signal abnormalities on MRI.
Progressive brainstem and corticobulbar involvement in EE encephalopathy impairs swallowing coordination.
Early-onset progressive metabolic encephalopathy and corticobulbar motor injury delay or abolish expressive speech acquisition.
Progressive pyramidal spasticity, dystonia, and encephalopathy prevent independent ambulation in severely affected children.
Catabolic stress during intercurrent infection increases endogenous sulfide and bioenergetic strain, accelerating encephalopathic injury.
